title: Grab And Move should work with TouchScreen & Stylus
author: JimR-15

judgment.rationale: The request describes a desired input modality but does not establish whether Windows emits a compatible pointer sequence, whether the configured modifier is observed during touch/stylus drag, or whether this is intended feature expansion rather than a regression.
evidence: The report says Win/Alt plus mouse drags windows, but the same gesture with touch or stylus does nothing.
Grab And Move currently installs a WH_MOUSE_LL hook and MouseProc handles WM_LBUTTONDOWN, WM_MOUSEMOVE, and WM_LBUTTONUP.
No comments, diagnostic archive, configuration details, or build version beyond 0.100.2 were provided.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a focused current-build comparison of mouse, touch, and pen input before designing a pointer-input implementation.

fix_assessment.rationale: The existing low-level mouse-hook implementation does not establish whether a PowerToys bug or unsupported pointer modality is being reported.

issue_context.summary: A touchscreen laptop user expects Grab And Move's modifier-plus-mouse gesture to move windows when performed with touch or a stylus.
known_information: Mouse activation works for the reporter.
Touch and stylus activation do not move a window.
Grab And Move presently processes low-level mouse button and movement messages.
inferences: Supporting touch and pen may require a distinct pointer-input path rather than a small change to mouse-hook handling.
issue_context.analysis: The reported behavior is plausible from the current input boundary, but the missing current-build and input-observation evidence determines whether this should be triaged as a feature request, regression, or pointer-routing defect.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue and its empty discussion.
Inspected src/modules/GrabAndMove/GrabAndMove/main.cpp; MouseProc is driven by WH_MOUSE_LL mouse messages.
Searched live PowerToys issues for a matching touch/stylus Grab And Move report and found no direct duplicate.

information_gaps.information: A current-build comparison showing whether Win/Alt is recognized and whether a mouse, finger, and pen each generate the expected drag behavior.
information_gaps.why_needed: It distinguishes unsupported pointer input from a modifier-state or regression defect.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On the latest PowerToys build, record a short screen capture while repeating the same title-bar drag with mouse, finger, and pen; include the configured activation modifier and Windows pen/touch settings.

comment.body: Thank you for the clear mouse-versus-touch comparison. Grab And Move currently receives low-level mouse drag messages, so we need to distinguish unsupported touch/pen routing from a modifier-state regression. Please test the latest PowerToys build and provide a short recording repeating the same title-bar drag with a mouse, finger, and stylus, along with the selected Grab And Move modifier and relevant Windows pen/touch settings. This will determine whether a pointer-input implementation is appropriate.
